from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        m_group = VGroup(block_m, label_m)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(collision_count, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Intuition", [
            "Phase space rotations yield discrete counts.",
            "Pi emerges from conservation laws.",
            "Geometry and physics are deeply linked."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in Phase Space diagram showing circular trajectories. Color: #FFFFFF.
        phase_diagram = Circle(radius=1.0, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(phase_diagram, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        label = Text("Phase Space", color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        label.next_to(phase_diagram, UP)
        self.play(FadeIn(phase_diagram), FadeIn(label))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash the intersection of geometry and physics nodes. Color: #00FFFF.
        node1 = Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(phase_diagram.get_center() + LEFT * 0.5)
        node2 = Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(phase_diagram.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.5)
        node3 = Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(phase_diagram.get_center() + UP * 0.5)
        
        node_label1 = Text("Physics", color="#00FFFF", font_size=16).next_to(node1, LEFT)
        node_label2 = Text("Geometry", color="#00FFFF", font_size=16).next_to(node2, RIGHT)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(node1), FadeIn(node2), FadeIn(node3), FadeIn(node_label1), FadeIn(node_label2))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out all elements to black background.
        self.play(FadeOut(phase_diagram), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(node1), FadeOut(node2), FadeOut(node3), FadeOut(node_label1), FadeOut(node_label2))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Digit Emergence
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of Newtonian mechanics

sections.title: The Hook: An Unexpected Discovery
sections.content: Introduce the counter-intuitive puzzle: How can a series of simple block collisions compute the digits of Pi? Present a visual of two blocks sliding on a frictionless surface towards a wall.
sections.example: A small block (mass m) and a large block (mass M=100m) sliding on a frictionless floor.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Briefly review Conservation of Momentum and Conservation of Kinetic Energy. Explain that elastic collisions between blocks follow these two laws, leading to a system of equations that define the velocity updates.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'phase space' plot where the velocity of block A is the x-axis and block B is the y-axis, forming a circular arc path.

sections.title: Geometric Mapping: The Circle Connection
sections.content: Explain that the velocity states of the two blocks can be mapped onto a circle. As collisions occur, the velocity vector rotates by a specific angle. The total number of collisions corresponds to the arc length covered, mapping to Pi.
sections.example: An animation showing the velocity vector rotating around a circle every time a collision occurs; the total rotation angle is proportional to the square root of the mass ratio.

sections.title: Scaling Powers of 100
sections.content: Demonstrate that as the mass ratio M/m increases by factors of 100 (100, 10,000, 1,000,000), the number of collisions matches the digits of Pi (3, 31, 314, etc.).
sections.example: A digital counter display next to the colliding blocks showing the digits '3.14...' ticking up as the mass of the larger block increases.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
sections.content: Synthesize why this works: The problem is a discrete manifestation of a continuous rotation in phase space. Conclude that Pi appears whenever we look at the 'geometry' of conservation laws.
sections.example: A final visual summary: 1. Set up blocks, 2. Count collisions, 3. Reveal Pi.
